pipelines.name: build-kb
pipelines.description: Build ONLY the knowledge base from a client's raw reference files, then STOP — this pipeline generates no document, no config, no other deliverable. It runs kb-builder alone to extract the delivery team's format, boilerplate, and product knowledge into a reusable KB, and returns that KB. Use it whenever the user wants JUST the KB and has NOT asked for a specific deliverable in the same request — e.g. 'build the KB for this client', 'onboard this client', 'set up the generator'. The KB it produces is the seed for every generation pipeline, so keep the session id it reports: later, pass that id as `seed_session_id` to document-from-kb or config-from-kb to generate a deliverable, or to output-feedback to refine the KB. Do NOT reach for document-agent or config-generator when the user only wants a KB — those append a generator step the user did not ask for.

pipelines.name: document-agent
pipelines.description: Produce a finished business document from raw reference files end to end. Runs kb-builder to extract the team's format and product knowledge into a KB, then document-generator to write and render the final document (PDF or DOCX) directly from that KB. This builds the KB AND produces a document in one run — so use it only when the user wants the finished document now. If the user wants ONLY the KB and no document yet, use build-kb instead; if the KB was already built by an earlier run, use document-from-kb to skip rebuilding it.

pipelines.name: document-from-kb
pipelines.description: Generate a finished business document (SOW, BRD, HLD, proposal, etc.) from an EXISTING knowledge base, WITHOUT rebuilding it. Use when the KB was already built by an earlier run and you just want another document from it for a new deal. This is the 'straight to generation' path that skips the kb-builder phase of document-agent. Point at the KB via `seed_session_id` — pass the pipeline session id of the earlier run that built the KB (the one it reported on completion); the server recovers that run's KB bucket from it automatically, so it is the only id you need. Pass the per-deal MOM/brief via `input_paths` (local paths) / `artifacts` / `urls` and describe the deal in `context`. The KB is staged in as read-only reference and the finished document is written to its own fresh output bucket — the KB is never modified.

pipelines.name: code-integration
pipelines.description: Integrate a platform into the USER'S OWN codebase end to end, starting from that platform's documentation. Runs kb-builder to ingest the SDK/API docs the user provides (an SDK reference, integration guide, OpenAPI spec, code samples — or `urls` to the published docs) and extract the callable surface into a KB (symbols, signatures, imports, idioms, language, conventions), then code-agent to write the integration strictly from that surface. Use when no KB exists yet — 'here are the {platform} docs, add it to my app'. If the KB was already built by an earlier run, use code-from-kb instead and skip re-reading the docs. THIS PIPELINE DOES NOT WRITE TO THE USER'S PROJECT: the server has no access to it. It returns the code plus an `integration.json` manifest in `output_dir`, and PAUSES asking YOU to apply that manifest in the user's working directory and report the build/lint result. Reply with the result via `session_id` + `response`; the skill repairs against the KB and pauses again, or finishes. IMPORTANT — attach ONLY the platform's documentation via `input_paths`/`artifacts`/`urls`: those reach the FIRST step, which is kb-builder, and it would absorb anything you hand it into the knowledge base. Do NOT attach the user's own source files here; that pollutes the KB with their codebase. Describe the target project in `context` instead — the target directory, the language and version, the dependency manifest, and two or three representative existing files quoted inline — because `context` reaches every step and is the only channel that gets the project to the code step. When you want to hand over real project files rather than describe them, build the KB first (build-kb or this pipeline) and then use code-from-kb, where code-agent is the first step and receives attachments directly.

pipelines.name: code-from-kb

Point at the KB via `seed_session_id` — the pipeline session id the earlier run reported on completion. THIS PIPELINE DOES NOT WRITE TO THE USER'S PROJECT: the server has no access to it. It returns the code plus an `integration.json` manifest in `output_dir`, and PAUSES asking YOU to apply that manifest in the user's working directory and report the build/lint result. Before the first call, gather the target directory, language, dependency manifest, and two or three representative existing files, and describe them in `context` — pass at most a NARROW subtree via `input_paths` (a directory is copied whole, so never pass a repo root with node_modules or .venv in it).

pipelines.name: output-feedback
pipelines.description: Turn a user's complaint about a generated OUTPUT into approved amendments to the knowledge base behind it, so the next generation is better. The user talks about the OUTPUT — 'the SOW is off-brand', 'the document missed a section', 'the config has the wrong value' — and need NOT mention the KB at all; this flow deliberately routes the fix to the KB, because every generator skill reads the KB at runtime, so correcting the KB is what actually fixes future outputs. Point it at the run whose output is at fault via `seed_session_id` — the pipeline session id that run reported on completion; the server resolves that run's KB bucket from it and refines it in place — and pass the flagged issues as `context`; optionally attach the defective output and/or a corrected version via `input_paths`/`urls`. Runs diagnose-bug in KB mode to analyse the KB against the feedback and propose amendments for review (adding a fact the KB never recorded, correcting one it recorded wrongly, or flagging a rule the KB already states correctly as a generator defect rather than restating it), then apply-fixes in KB mode to write the approved amendments back into that same KB in place. The KB is edited on disk with no git commit; the amended KB is written back into its own outputs/mcp bucket in place so every skill that reads it at runtime picks up the improvement.

the document you produced is off-brand or incomplete

pipelines.name: map-website-kb
pipelines.description: Map a LIVE WEBSITE into a knowledge base and STOP — this pipeline runs no automation and carries out no task on the site. Use when the user gives a URL and wants the site understood and documented so it can be automated later: it runs kb-builder in site-mapping mode, which drives a real browser over the site, walks the user journeys in scope, and records the screens, URL patterns, element locators, success and failure cues, waits, and the human gates (login, MFA, CAPTCHA, payment) that stand in the way. Pass the site as `url` (or in `context`), and pass the SOW naming which journeys matter via `input_paths`/`artifacts` — the SOW only SCOPES which flows get walked; it is never absorbed into the KB, so the resulting KB stays reusable for future workflows against the same site. Mapping is read-only by default: it will pause and ask before submitting any form or changing any state, and before signing in to an account. Keep the session id it reports — pass it later as `seed_session_id` to browser-run-from-kb to actually execute a workflow. Do NOT use this when the user wants the task performed now; that is browser-automation.

pipelines.name: browser-automation
pipelines.description: Automate a workflow on a website end to end when there is NO API available — map the site, then actually carry the task out in a live browser. Runs kb-builder in site-mapping mode to drive a real browser over the URL and build a web-flow KB (screens, locators, cues, waits, human gates), then browser-agent to execute the SOW's workflow live against that site: navigating, clicking, filling, asserting each step's success cue, and capturing results. This MAPS the site AND performs the work in one run, so use it only when the user wants the task done now. If the user only wants the site understood, use map-website-kb; if the site was already mapped by an earlier run, use browser-run-from-kb to skip re-mapping. Pass the site as `url` and the SOW via `input_paths`/`artifacts` — and ALSO describe the workflow to carry out in `context`, because only the first step receives the caller's attachments, so `context` is what reaches the execution step. It is interactive by design and will pause to ask whenever it needs a credential, an OTP or MFA code, a signup decision, a payment authorization, or a go-ahead before anything that changes state on the site; production is never targeted silently.

pipelines.name: browser-run-from-kb
pipelines.description: Execute a workflow LIVE in a browser from an EXISTING web-flow knowledge base, WITHOUT re-mapping the site. Use when the site was already mapped by an earlier run and you just want another workflow carried out against it — the 'straight to execution' path that skips the mapping phase of browser-automation. This is the common steady state: map a site once, then run many different SOWs against it. Point at the KB via `seed_session_id` — the pipeline session id of the earlier run that mapped the site (the one it reported on completion); the server recovers that run's KB bucket from it automatically. Pass the workflow to run via `input_paths`/`artifacts` (the SOW) and any per-run values in `context`. The SOW is the single input document and carries the environment values and credentials too, so attach it as a FILE rather than pasting it into `context` — file inputs reach the skill without going through the conversation, and its contents are never quoted back or written into the run record. The KB is staged in read-only and is never modified; the run record (what ran, what changed, what was captured, redacted) is written to a fresh output bucket. browser-agent drives the site strictly from the KB — it never invents a page or selector, never solves a CAPTCHA, and pauses to ask for credentials, one-time codes, or a go-ahead before any action that changes state. If the site has drifted since it was mapped, the run stops and reports the gap rather than improvising; re-map with map-website-kb to fix it.

pipelines.name: design-api-lld
pipelines.description: Turn a platform's own API DOCUMENTATION into a reviewable execution plan and STOP — this pipeline calls nothing, touches no credential, and binds no environment. Runs kb-builder to ingest the API docs the user provides (an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, a Postman collection, API reference pages or PDFs, integration guides — or `urls` pointing at the published docs) and extract the contract into a KB (auth scheme, endpoints, methods, request/response schemas, status codes, pagination, rate limits, idempotency), then api-agent to resolve that KB plus the SOW into an LLD/ED — a Low-Level Design / Execution Document: an ordered, fully-specified, SELF-CONTAINED runbook a Runner later executes. Pass the API docs via `input_paths`/`artifacts`/`urls` and the SOW via `input_paths` — and ALSO describe the workflow to automate in `context`, because only the FIRST step receives the caller's attachments, so `context` is what reaches the design step. The LLD names the credentials the Runner will need BY NAME only and lists the environments without binding one. Use this when the plan should be read and approved before anything runs; use api-automation to design and run in one go. Keep the session id it reports: pass it as `seed_session_id` to api-lld-from-kb to design another workflow off the same KB, and execute the LLD with run-lld.

pipelines.name: api-automation
pipelines.description: Automate a workflow against a platform's REST API end to end — read the API docs, design the plan, then actually make the live calls. Runs kb-builder to extract the API contract from the documentation the user provides into a KB, api-agent to design the LLD/ED (the ordered execution plan), and runner-agent to EXECUTE it live as real HTTP requests: authenticating, managing the token lifecycle, chaining each response into the next request, and handling retries, rate limits, pagination and partial failure. This designs AND performs the work in one run, so use it only when the user wants the calls made now. If the plan should be reviewed first, use design-api-lld and then run-lld. This lane is for platforms that HAVE an API; when the only surface is the screen, use browser-automation instead. Pass the API docs via `input_paths`/`artifacts`/`urls` and the SOW via `input_paths` — and ALSO describe the workflow in `context`, because only the FIRST step receives the caller's attachments, so `context` is what reaches the design and execution steps. It is interactive by design and will PAUSE to ask: it picks the environment (defaulting to non-prod — prod/live is always an explicit, surfaced choice), asks in chat for each credential VALUE by the name the design lists, confirms before every state-changing call, double-confirms destructive ones against the concrete target, and stops rather than cascading on a broken chain. Because only the first step gets attachments, credentials cannot be attached as a file here — the Runner asks for them in the conversation; if you would rather keep a secret out of chat, run design-api-lld first and hand the secrets file to run-lld instead. A redacted run record (run.log + result.json) is written to the output bucket.

pipelines.name: api-lld-from-kb
pipelines.description: Design an LLD/ED — the ordered execution document a Runner later carries out — from an EXISTING knowledge base, WITHOUT re-ingesting the API documentation. Use when the KB was already built by an earlier run and you want another workflow planned against the same platform; this is the 'straight to design' path that skips the kb-builder phase of design-api-lld. Point at the KB via `seed_session_id` — the pipeline session id of the earlier run that built it (the one it reported on completion); the server recovers that run's KB bucket automatically and stages it read-only, so the KB is never modified. Pass the SOW via `input_paths`/`artifacts` and any per-run values in `context`; because api-agent is the FIRST step here, attachments reach it directly. NOTHING IS EXECUTED: no call is made, no credential value is read or requested, and no environment is bound — the LLD names the credentials the Runner will need by name only and lists the KB's environments as options, instructing the Runner to default to non-prod. If the KB documents an operation the SOW asks for but the docs never described, the design says so rather than inventing an endpoint. Execute the result with run-lld.

pipelines.name: run-lld
pipelines.description: Execute an LLD/ED — a Low-Level Design / Execution Document an earlier design run produced — as a live run, carrying it out exactly as written. Pass the LLD ITSELF as a file via `input_paths` (plus any per-run values in `context`). Do NOT pass `seed_session_id`: the Runner reads the LLD and nothing else — never the KB, never the SOW — so it must not be handed a knowledge base. This is the second half of design-api-lld: design once, review the plan, then run it here, as many times as needed. The Runner owns what the design deliberately left open — it PICKS the environment (defaulting to the LLD's non-prod one; prod/live is always an explicit, surfaced choice) and SOURCES the credential VALUES by the exact names the LLD lists. Attach a secrets/env file via `input_paths` alongside the LLD and it reaches the skill without passing through the conversation; otherwise the Runner PAUSES and asks for each missing value by name in chat. It also honors the LLD's safety gates: it presents the whole plan first, waits for a go-ahead before the first state-changing call, re-confirms destructive steps against the concrete target, stops on a broken chain instead of chaining a blank, and stops rather than cascading on partial failure. It writes a redacted run record (run.log + result.json + per-step evidence) to the output bucket and never prints a secret. If the LLD is defective — a step pointing at the KB, or a missing mechanic — it STOPS and reports rather than improvising; fix that by re-running the design, not by patching the document. This lane executes HTTP/API plans; a browser-surface plan is not run here (this step is given no browser) — use browser-run-from-kb or browser-automation for web-UI work.
